title: HCP — Relinquish Own Grant — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Relinquish own grant operation (HCP 5.2.7; `DELETE /v2/grants/{grantId}` with a Context Client's token for that grant in HCP 9.2): an HCP Client gives up the grant under which it acts. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

grantId.description: HCP `grantId` (the `{grantId}` path parameter of HCP 9.2): the grant to relinquish, which MUST be the grant `accessToken` was issued under; any other fails with `permissionDenied` (HCP 5.2.7).

accessToken.description: The HCP access token for the grant under which the client acts (HCP 12, 13), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP Binding sends it as a Bearer token (HCP 9.3); this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Response.title: HCP — Relinquish Own Grant — response payload
Response.description: The grant is relinquished. HCP defines no result and its HTTP Binding answers `204 No Content` (HCP 5.2.7, 9.4.6), so the payload is the empty object. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.
